attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them. If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero, meaning no projection of one onto the other. A negative dot product indicates the angle between them is greater than 90°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points opposite to the vector’s direction.
